subject: Linguistics
title: Head-Initial Versus Head-Final
description: A 60-second lesson on Head-Initial Versus Head-Final.

hook.text: English says 'eat sushi'—verb then object. Japanese says 'sushi eat'—object then verb.

buildup.text: In head-initial languages the head of a phrase comes first; in head-final, the head comes last.

discovery.text: This parameter tends to be consistent: head-initial languages put prepositions before nouns too.

twist.text: Head-final languages use postpositions instead: 'Tokyo to' rather than 'to Tokyo.'

climax.text: This single parameter predicts a cascade of word-order differences across the entire grammar.

punchline.text: One setting—head first or last—shapes the whole language.

quiz.question: What does head-final mean?
options: The head of a phrase comes last
